provider: IPFS Foundation public gateways (ipfs.io / dweb.link / trustless-gateway.link)

free_tier.stated: No storage at all. Gateway only. And the gateway itself is being retired: ipfs.io/dweb.link return HTTP 429 with 'Retry-After: 900' and 'Sunset: Mon, 21 Sep 2026', and redirect browsers to inbrowser.link.
free_tier.notes: Headline offer; binding constraint specified in limits.

per_object_cap.stated: No per-object cap documented in published terms; absence is not an unlimited claim.
per_object_cap.notes: extraction found no per-object clause; some of these providers meter on object count rather than bytes, and some state no cap

retention.stated: No retention statement documented in published terms; absence is not an unlimited claim.
retention.notes: extraction found no retention clause; the seed's limits text may still state one, see extras.limits_verbatim

egress.terms: Rate-limited to the point of unusability from a datacenter IP: 10/10 requests returned 429 on a cold burst, and a single request after a 5 s pause also returned 429. Published posture: 'Rate limiting has begun on ipfs.io and dweb.link for hotlinked and backend traffic, and will be increasing.' Docs: 'no SLA, no support, and shared rate limits that can throttle or block your traffic at any time, without notice.'

tooling: curl/any HTTP client; path gateway at ipfs.io, subdomain at dweb.link; trustless subset at trustless-gateway.link.
chaining: none. The three hostnames are one backend: 'They are not three separate services... sharing the same cache, the same connections to the IPFS network, and the same rate limits.' Rotating hostnames burns the same budget.
limits_note: 429 + Retry-After 900 observed on the first request; Range requests capped at 5 GiB (Cloudflare CDN limit); Sunset header 2026-09-21.

identity_cost.detail: no identity_cost field and no identity statement in the source record; defaulted to email and flagged, not evidence

reliability_note: This is the single most important measurement in the slot: the 'free IPFS CDN' that every tutorial assumes is (a) gone as of 2026-09-21 and (b) already 429-ing datacenter IPs before that date. Any architecture that depends on ipfs.io/dweb.link for serving is dead on arrival.
